subproblem.title: τ(M, θ, ξ) has the measure representation (Hᵏ⌞M, θξ)
subproblem.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, Hᵏ := μHE[k] on ℝ^P = Eucl P, and let U ⊆ ℝ^P be any set. Let M ⊆ ℝ^P, θ : ℝ^P → ℝ and ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_k(ℝ^P) (k-vectors, NVector (Eucl P) k) satisfy IsRectifiableTriple U k M θ ξ, and let X ∈ D_k(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U k) satisfy X(ω) = τ(M, θ, ξ)(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) dHᵏ(x) (tauAction k M θ ξ ω) for every test form ω ∈ D^k(U) (TestFormOn U k). Then (Hᵏ⌞M, θξ) is a measure representation of X, i.e. IsMeasureRepresentation X (μHE[k].restrict M) (x ↦ θ(x) • ξ(x)): for every ω ∈ D^k(U) the function x ↦ (θ(x) • ξ(x))(ω(x)) is Hᵏ⌞M-integrable and X(ω) = ∫ (θ(x) • ξ(x))(ω(x)) d(Hᵏ⌞M)(x).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (U M : Set (Eucl P)) (θ : Eucl P → ℝ) (ξ : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) k) (X : GeometricCurrentOn U k), IsRectifiableTriple U k M θ ξ → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U k, X ω = tauAction k M θ ξ ω) → IsMeasureRepresentation X ((μHE[k] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict M) (fun x => θ x • ξ x)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝ^P := Eucl P. H := Hᵏ := μHE[k]. D_k(U) := GeometricCurrentOn U k and D^k(U) := TestFormOn U k: smooth k-forms on ℝ^P with compact support and tsupport ⊆ U. τ(M, θ, ξ)(ω) := tauAction k M θ ξ ω = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) dH(x). k-vectors are elements of NVector (Eucl P) k, the continuous linear functionals on k-covectors. For t ∈ ℝ and a k-vector w, (t • w)(α) = t·w(α).

Source. This is preliminary (ii) of the parent proof: (H⌞M, θξ) is a measure representation of τ(M, θ, ξ).

Statement. Let U ⊆ ℝ^P be any set, let IsRectifiableTriple U k M θ ξ hold, and let X ∈ D_k(U) satisfy X(ω) = τ(M, θ, ξ)(ω) for every ω ∈ D^k(U). Then IsMeasureRepresentation X (H⌞M) (x ↦ θ(x) • ξ(x)). That is, for every ω ∈ D^k(U):
- x ↦ (θ(x) • ξ(x))(ω(x)) is H⌞M-integrable; and
- X(ω) = ∫ (θ(x) • ξ(x))(ω(x)) d(H⌞M)(x).

1. (The test form.) Fix ω ∈ D^k(U) and write ω also for its underlying form ℝ^P → Λᵏ(ℝ^P).
   - Membership in TestFormOn U k means ω is C^∞ with compact support and tsupport ω ⊆ U.
   - In particular ω is continuous (C^∞ ⇒ continuous) and HasCompactSupport ω.

2. (Integrability.) The sibling `ltg_tau_integrable`, second conjunct, applies to the continuous, compactly supported covector field ω with tsupport ω ⊆ U and the rectifiable triple (M, θ, ξ). It shows that h(x) := θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) is H-integrable on M, i.e. H⌞M-integrable.

3. (Pointwise identity.) For every x, (θ(x) • ξ(x))(ω(x)) = θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) = h(x). This holds because scalar multiplication of continuous linear functionals is pointwise (`smul_apply`, `smul_eq_mul`). So the two functions of x are equal (funext), and the integrability in the first bullet of the statement is step 2.

4. (Integral formula.) By the hypothesis on X and the definition of tauAction, X(ω) = τ(M, θ, ξ)(ω) = ∫_M h dH = ∫ h d(H⌞M). By step 3 this equals ∫ (θ(x) • ξ(x))(ω(x)) d(H⌞M)(x).

5. Since ω was arbitrary, steps 2–4 give both conjuncts of IsMeasureRepresentation for every ω ∈ D^k(U). ∎

Formalization notes (a complete Lean proof of exactly this statement compiled in a scratch build of frozen commit d8d46c9, with the sibling as a stub): `ω.2 : (IsSmoothForm ω ∧ HasCompactSupport ω) ∧ tsupport ω ⊆ U`; continuity is `ω.2.1.1.continuous`. Use `(Submission.ltg_tau_integrable P k U M θ ξ htr).2 ω hcont ω.2.1.2 ω.2.2`. Rewrite the integrand with `funext x; simp only [smul_apply, smul_eq_mul]`; `ContinuousLinearMap.smul_apply` is deprecated in favour of `smul_apply`. The integral formula is then `rfl` after `rw [hrep ω]`.
proof_key_steps: A test form ω ∈ D^k(U) is continuous, has compact support and tsupport ω ⊆ U.
The sibling ltg_tau_integrable (second conjunct) gives Hᵏ-integrability of x ↦ θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) on M.
(θ(x) • ξ(x))(ω(x)) = θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) pointwise, so the integrability transfers to x ↦ (θ(x) • ξ(x))(ω(x)) for Hᵏ⌞M, and X(ω) = τ(M, θ, ξ)(ω) = ∫ (θ • ξ)(ω) d(Hᵏ⌞M).

audit.reason: The proof directly establishes both fields of IsMeasureRepresentation using tau_integrable and the pointwise identity (θ • ξ)(ω) = θ·ξ(ω). No existence, openness or measurability hypothesis is silently added.
